Abraham Gottlob Werner was a German geologist who, in the late 1700s, developed a standardized color-naming system so mineralogists could describe rock and mineral color consistently. In 1814 (2nd ed. 1821), Scottish flower painter Patrick Syme illustrated and expanded Werner's system into **110 named colors, organized into 10 classifications** (White, Grey, Black, Blue, Purple, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red, Brown) -- each cross-referenced against an animal, a plant, and a mineral where that color occurs in nature. Charles Darwin carried a copy on the *Beagle* to describe organisms and landscapes with a shared, precise color vocabulary.

Palette Jack's Werner mode lets you filter by classification and pull a randomized set of these historical colors as a ready-to-paste hex list -- useful for quick categorical palettes, or just for the pleasure of finding out your data happens to be "Arterial Blood Red" or "Skimmed-milk White."

## The classifications

```{r}
#| label: load-werner
#| message: false
#| results: asis
library(tidyverse)
library(glue)

werner <- read_csv("../data/werner-colors.csv")

swatch_html <- function(hex, name, cap = 8) {
  n <- length(hex)
  hex <- head(hex, cap)
  name <- head(name, cap)
  spans <- glue('<span class="mini-swatch" style="background:{hex}" title="{name}"></span>')
  out <- paste(spans, collapse = "")
  if (n > cap) out <- paste0(out, glue('<span class="palette-module-more">+{n - cap} more</span>'))
  out
}

gallery <- werner |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    n_colors = n(),
    examples = paste(head(name, 4), collapse = ", "),
    swatches = swatch_html(hex, name),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(group)

cat(
  '<div class="palette-gallery">',
  glue_data(
    gallery,
    '<div class="palette-module">
  <h4>{group} <span class="palette-module-count">{n_colors} colors</span></h4>
  <p class="palette-module-desc">e.g. {examples}</p>
  <div class="palette-module-swatches">{swatches}</div>
</div>'
  ),
  '</div>',
  sep = "\n"
)
```

## How to use it

1. Pick a **classification** below (or leave it on "All classifications").
2. Drag the **slider** to choose how many colors you want -- it caps at 12, since legibility drops off past that point (see citations below).
3. Click **Randomize**, then copy the R vector -- or the plain hex list -- straight into your plot.

## Try it

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
data = FileAttachment("../data/werner-colors.csv").csv({typed: true})
groupNames = Array.from(new Set(data.map(d => d.group))).sort()
groupOptions = ["All classifications", ...groupNames]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof groupChoice = Inputs.select(groupOptions, {label: "Classification", value: "All classifications"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
filtered = groupChoice === "All classifications" ? data : data.filter(d => d.group === groupChoice)
maxN = Math.min(12, filtered.length)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof n = Inputs.range([1, maxN], {label: "Number of colors", step: 1, value: Math.min(5, maxN)})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof shuffleSeed = Inputs.button("Randomize", {value: 0, reduce: v => v + 1})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sample = {
  shuffleSeed;
  return d3.shuffle(filtered.slice()).slice(0, n);
}
hexList = sample.map(d => d.hex).join("\n")
hexVector = 'c(' + sample.map(d => `"${d.hex}"`).join(', ') + ')'
hexSingleQuote = sample.map(d => `'${d.hex}'`).join(', ')
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function textColor(hex) {
  const c = hex.replace("#", "");
  const r = parseInt(c.substring(0, 2), 16);
  const g = parseInt(c.substring(2, 4), 16);
  const b = parseInt(c.substring(4, 6), 16);
  const lum = (0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b) / 255;
  return lum > 0.6 ? "#241C1C" : "#FFFFFF";
}

html`<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(150px,1fr));gap:12px;margin:1.5rem 0;">
  ${sample.map(d => html`<div class="color-chip" style="background:${d.hex};padding:12px;min-height:96px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:flex-end;color:${textColor(d.hex)}">
    <div style="font-weight:600;">${d.hex}</div>
    <div style="font-size:.82rem;">${d.name}</div>
  </div>`)}
</div>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
vectorCopyBtn = {
  const label = () => `Copy R vector (${sample.length})`;
  const btn = html`<button class="swatch-copy-btn">${label()}</button>`;
  btn.onclick = () => {
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(hexVector).then(() => {
      btn.textContent = "Copied!";
      setTimeout(() => { btn.textContent = label(); }, 1200);
    });
  };
  return btn;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
listCopyBtn = {
  const label = () => `Copy hex list (${sample.length})`;
  const btn = html`<button class="swatch-copy-btn swatch-copy-btn--secondary">${label()}</button>`;
  btn.onclick = () => {
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(hexList).then(() => {
      btn.textContent = "Copied!";
      setTimeout(() => { btn.textContent = label(); }, 1200);
    });
  };
  return btn;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<div style="margin-top:1.5rem;">
  <p style="font-weight:600;margin-bottom:.4rem;">1. Ready for <code>scale_fill_manual()</code></p>
  ${vectorCopyBtn}
  <pre class="hex-list-block"><span class="hl-fu">c</span>(${sample.map((d, i) => html`<span class="hl-st">"${d.hex}"</span>${i < sample.length - 1 ? ", " : ""}`)})</pre>
</div>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
singleQuoteCopyBtn = {
  const label = () => `Copy quoted hex (${sample.length})`;
  const btn = html`<button class="swatch-copy-btn swatch-copy-btn--secondary">${label()}</button>`;
  btn.onclick = () => {
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(hexSingleQuote).then(() => {
      btn.textContent = "Copied!";
      setTimeout(() => { btn.textContent = label(); }, 1200);
    });
  };
  return btn;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<div style="margin-top:1.25rem;">
  <p style="font-weight:600;margin-bottom:.4rem;">2. Or just the hex codes</p>
  ${listCopyBtn}
  <pre class="hex-list-block">${hexList}</pre>
</div>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<div style="margin-top:1.25rem;">
  <p style="font-weight:600;margin-bottom:.4rem;">3. Or as quoted strings</p>
  ${singleQuoteCopyBtn}
  <pre class="hex-list-block">${hexSingleQuote}</pre>
</div>`
```
